newsitem.title: USA: Koll Real Estate files for Chapter 11.
newsitem.headline: Koll Real Estate files for Chapter 11.

text.p: Koll Real Estate Group Inc KREG.OB on Monday filed for Chapter 11 protection from its creditors in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware, court papers say.
On Friday the company said 95 percent of the holders of its stock and bonds had already approved a prepackaged reorganization plan for emerging from bankruptcy protection.
Koll, a real estate holding company based in Newport Beach, California, listed assets of $272.2 million and liabilities of $271.1 million, court papers say.
The company listed $339.2 million in fixed liquidated secured debt, including intercompany balances, with 8,370 holders.

Among the 20 largest unsecured creditors are trustee First National Association of St. Paul, Minnesota, with $164.6 million in 12 percent senior subordinated pay-in-kind debentures due 2002; trustee Bank of New York Co Inc, with $41.1 million in the 12% notes; Guaranty Federal Bank FSB of Dallas, Texas, with a $56.5 million contingent guaranty; and Bank One Texas of Dallas, with a $56.9 million contingent guaranty.
Koll listed 67 wholly owned subsidiaries worldwide which are not part of the bankruptcy filing.
Bridge Partners LP of Greenwich, Connecticut, owns 11.5 percent of class A common stock and 30.5 percent of series A convertible preferred stock, court papers say.
